more_info.overview: Red 2G is a synthetic azo colour specified as a disodium salt of an acetamido-substituted naphthalene dye. Its colouring function is to add or restore colour in the food. The available identity record does not establish a typical retail-food example for this exact preparation. Commercial specifications and legal conditions need to refer to the particular substance or preparation named here.
more_info.daily_intake: Historical ADI: 0–0.1 mg/kg body weight (JECFA, 1981). Codex food-use provisions were withdrawn in 2018.
more_info.banned_in:
Banned in: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden.
Codex food-use provisions were withdrawn in 2018; JECFA did not re-evaluate the dye that year.
EU use as a food colour, marketing and imports of foods containing Red 2G were suspended in 2007; the current EU food list checked in 2026 does not restore this food permission.
